note: Bibliographic records/Wilde bibliography: first in Oxford magazine The Chameleon, Dec 1894. Separate pirated printings by Smithers c. 1905-06.

title: The Heat of the Day
author: Elizabeth Bowen
note: National Library of Ireland catalogue: Knopf, New York, 1948 (original). UK first edition Jonathan Cape is 1949; some sources give only 1949. Library year is the US first.

title: Chinmoku (Silence)
author: Shūsaku Endō
note: Wikipedia/Wikidata: Chinmoku, Shinchosha 1966, won Tanizaki Prize; English translation by William Johnston, Peter Owen 1969.

title: The Poems of Emily Dickinson (Johnson edition)
author: Emily Dickinson (edited by Thomas H. Johnson)
note: Results confirm Johnson's 3-vol Belknap/Harvard edition but I saw no snippet stating the year. From memory: 1955 (3 vols, Belknap Press); one-volume Complete Poems 1960.

title: Clarissa
author: Samuel Richardson
note: Britannica/others: issued in instalments, vols 1-2 Nov 1747, 3-4 Apr 1748, 5-7 Dec 1748. Library's 1748 matches completion/title pages; first publication began 1747.
resolution: The library gives the completion year (1748); publication began in November 1747. Left as is.

title: The Redress of Poetry
author: Seamus Heaney
note: National Library of Ireland record: Faber and Faber, London, 1995 (Oxford Lectures). Lectures given 1989-94; the first appeared as an OUP pamphlet in 1990 (PN Review).

title: Al-Mutasha’il (The Secret Life of Saeed the Pessoptimist)
author: Emile Habibi
note: Wikipedia and teaching pages: Arabic novel 1974; full Arabic title al-Waqa'i' al-gharība fī ikhtifā' Sa'īd Abī al-Nahs al-Mutashā'il. English trans. 1985 (Zed). Original publisher sources vary.

title: Daisy Jones & The Six
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
note: Wikipedia and many library catalogue records: Ballantine Books, 5 March 2019.

title: Walk Two Moons
author: Sharon Creech
note: Wikipedia: HarperCollins first edition 12 June 1994 (BookBrowse says 1 May 1994); won 1995 Newbery Medal.

title: Smilla's Sense of Snow
author: Peter Høeg
note: Wikipedia/encyclopedia.com: Danish original Frøken Smillas fornemmelse for sne, 1992; English editions 1993 (UK title Miss Smilla's Feeling for Snow). 1992 is the Danish year.

title: The Heptameron
author: Marguerite de Navarre
note: Wikipedia/Gutenberg preface: first printing Paris 1558 as Histoires des amans fortunez (67 tales, ed. Boaistuau); title Heptaméron only in Gruget's 1559 edition. Author d. 1549.

title: Rendezvous with Rama
author: Arthur C. Clarke
note: Encyclopedic summaries and Goodreads (1 June 1973); rare-book dealers cite Harcourt (US) and Gollancz (UK) 1973 first editions. One Spanish bookseller says 1972, likely an error.

title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
note: Wikipedia: UK publication 5 Jan 1886, Longmans, Green. A rare-book dealer says the first US edition (Scribner) came out days earlier, also 1886.

title: The Bourne Identity
author: Robert Ludlum
note: Wikipedia: Richard Marek, February 1980; a rare-book dealer lists the first edition as New York: Richard Marek, 1980.

title: The Clouds
author: Aristophanes
note: Furman University dramaturgy page: first performed at the City Dionysia in 423 BCE (placed third); surviving text is a later revision. Date is first performance, not publication.

title: The Country Wife
author: William Wycherley
note: Wikipedia and a Nick Hern edition: premiere Jan 1675 (King's Company, Drury Lane); a Lafayette College edition says published 1675. Some listings say 1672; written c. 1671-72.

title: The Grand Sophy
author: Georgette Heyer
note: Wikipedia: first published 1950 by Heinemann (UK) and Putnam (US); a Heyer blog notes she was writing it in Nov 1949.

title: The Jungle
author: Upton Sinclair
note: Wikipedia: book form Doubleday, Page, 26 Feb 1906. It ran as a serial in Appeal to Reason in 1905, so 1906 is the book date, 1905 the serial.

title: The Midwich Cuckoos
author: John Wyndham
note: Wikipedia and a bookseller's first-edition listing: Michael Joseph, London, 1957.

title: The Monkey's Paw
author: W. W. Jacobs
note: Wikipedia summary: first in Harper's Monthly, September 1902, then in the collection The Lady of the Barge the same year.

title: The Palm-Wine Drinkard
author: Amos Tutuola
note: Wikipedia/EBSCO-type summaries: Faber and Faber, London, 1952; US edition Grove Press 1953; French translation by Queneau 1953.

title: The Pickwick Papers
author: Charles Dickens
note: Wikipedia and Britannica: serialised March 1836 to November 1837, book form 1837. Library's 1836 is the serial start; the one-volume book is 1837.

title: The Pilgrim's Progress
author: John Bunyan
note: Wikipedia: a 1678 allegory, entered in the Term Catalogue 18 Feb 1678 (registered Dec 1677); Part Two 1684.

title: Verse
author: Adelaide Crapsey
note: Cinquain.org/Wikipedia/Gutenberg-type results: Verse, Manas Press, Rochester NY, 1915 (posthumous, 28 cinquains); Knopf 2nd ed. 1922. Britannica calls it 'Verses'.

title: The Hundred-Year-Old Man Who Climbed Out of the Window and Disappeared
author: Jonas Jonasson
note: Wikipedia: Swedish original 9 Sept 2009 (Piratforlaget); English translation (Rod Bradbury) 12 July 2012. Library's 2009 is the Swedish first publication.

title: Tevye der milkhiker (Tevye the Dairyman)
author: Sholem Aleichem
note: Wikipedia 'Tevye': first published 1894. Wikipedia 'Dos groyse gevins' says written 1894, printed 1895 in Der hoyz-fraynd. Sources disagree by a year; 'c.' covers it.

title: The Song of Roland (La Chanson de Roland)
author: Anonymous (the closing lines name a Turold)
sourceYear: c. 1100 (early version c. 1040; added to c. 1115)
note: Britannica: composed about 1100. Wikipedia: early version c. 1040, reworked to c. 1115; sole Oxford MS 1129-65. Turold attribution debated, as the library says.

title: The Cold Equations
author: Tom Godwin
note: Wikipedia, SF Encyclopedia and Lightspeed results: first published in Astounding, August 1954, edited by John W. Campbell.

title: Tirukkural
author: Tiruvalluvar
sourceYear: c. 500 CE (disputed: 300 BCE to 6th c. CE)
note: Wikipedia 'Dating the Tirukkural': Blackburn gives scholarly consensus c. 500 CE, Zvelebil 450-500. Traditional and older views go much earlier, to 300 BCE; dating is contested.

title: The Magicians
author: Lev Grossman
note: Wikipedia entry and retail/library listings: Viking, 2009 (ISBN 978-0-670-02055-3); sequels 2011 and 2014.

title: Une saison en enfer
author: Arthur Rimbaud
note: Wikipedia and rare-book dealers: Brussels, Alliance Typographique (Poot), 1873, self-financed; written April-August 1873.

title: The Guernsey Literary and Potato Peel Pie Society
author: Mary Ann Shaffer and Annie Barrows
note: Wikipedia: Dial Press, 2008; BookBrowse gives 29 July 2008. Shaffer died Feb 2008; her niece Annie Barrows finished the book and is co-author.

title: The Rings of Saturn
author: W. G. Sebald
note: Search summary: German original 'Die Ringe des Saturn' (Eichborn, Frankfurt) 1995; first English edition Harvill Press 1998, trans. Michael Hulse. Library's 1995 is the German original.

title: Embassytown
author: China Miéville
note: Wikipedia: UK (Pan Macmillan) April/May 2011; US (Del Rey) 17 May 2011 per Goodreads/BookBrowse. Won the 2012 Locus Award for SF novel.

title: Flight to Canada
author: Ishmael Reed
note: Wikipedia and EBSCO/bookseller results: a 1976 novel by Ishmael Reed, Random House first edition.

title: The Raven
author: Edgar Allan Poe
note: Smithsonian National Postal Museum page and other results: first printed in the New York Evening Mirror, 29 January 1845.

title: The Road to Wigan Pier
author: George Orwell
note: Wikipedia and bookseller pages: first published 8 March 1937 by Gollancz (Left Book Club selection and trade edition); fifth Orwell book. First US edition 1958.

title: The Scarlet Letter
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
note: Wikipedia/EBSCO/rare-book pages: first published 16 March 1850, Ticknor, Reed & Fields, Boston. Author shown in page titles/URLs (summary text did not repeat his name).

title: The Shepheardes Calender
author: Edmund Spenser
note: Folger collection page and Wikisource title page: first edition 1579, printed by Hugh Singleton, London; pseudonymous 'Immerito', glosses by E.K.

title: The Song of Hiawatha
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
note: Wikipedia and rare-book pages: published 10 November 1855 by Ticknor and Fields, Boston (first printing dated October 1855 by one dealer). Written 1854-55.

title: The Sun Also Rises
author: Ernest Hemingway
note: Bookseller/publisher pages: published 22 October 1926 by Scribner's (first printing 5,090); UK edition 1927 as Fiesta (Jonathan Cape).

title: The Way of the World
author: William Congreve
note: Wikipedia, Gutenberg, publisher blurbs: first performed 1700 (March per one source) at Lincoln's Inn Fields and printed the same year by Jacob Tonson.

title: Tristram Shandy
author: Laurence Sterne
note: Wikipedia and library pages: vols 1-2 appeared 1759 (York, Ann Ward); full nine vols to 1767. Wikisource lists vol I as 1760 (imprint date); 1759 is the common date.

title: Twelfth Night
author: William Shakespeare
note: RSC and Internet Shakespeare: written c. 1601; first recorded performance 2 Feb 1602 (Middle Temple); first printed in the 1623 First Folio. Library year matches the composition date.

title: Utopia
author: Thomas More
note: History Today, St John's Cambridge, Low Countries articles: first printed Leuven (Dirk Martens), late/December 1516, ed. Erasmus and Peter Giles. Written in Latin 1515-16.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
author: Arthur C. Clarke
note: Wikipedia and bookseller pages: novel published 1968 (June per Wikipedia; Hutchinson UK, New American Library US); month varies by source. Written alongside Kubrick's film.

title: A Confederacy of Dunces
author: John Kennedy Toole
note: Wikipedia and rare-book dealers: first published 1980 by Louisiana State University Press (foreword by Walker Percy), posthumously; Pulitzer Prize 1981.

title: The Jataka Tales
author: Anonymous (Buddhist tradition)
sourceYear: 3rd-1st c. BCE (present form); range 5th c. BCE to 5th c. CE
note: Wikipedia/EBSCO: no named author; dates vary widely (verse core 5th c. BCE, commentary c. 5th c. CE). c. 200 BCE lies inside the 3rd-1st c. BCE range given for the stories' present form.

title: The Deal
author: Elle Kennedy
note: Boston Globe profile and library catalogue: self-published 2015 (KDP/Draft2Digital) as first Off-Campus book; Bloom Books reissue 2021. Library year is the original 2015 release.

title: The Bridge
author: Hart Crane
note: Wikipedia/EBSCO/Columbia: first published 1930, Black Sun Press (Paris, limited edition), then Boni & Liveright in New York. Conceived 1923.

title: Doonesbury
author: Garry Trudeau
note: Wikipedia/Andrews McMeel: syndicated daily debut 26 October 1970 (Universal Press Syndicate); it grew from Bull Tales in the Yale Daily News, begun 1968.

title: Of Being Numerous
author: George Oppen
note: Poetry Foundation, poets.org, NII catalogue, LRB: published 1968 by New Directions; Pulitzer Prize for Poetry 1969.

title: Rashomon
author: Akira Kurosawa (director)
note: Wikipedia, TCM, Japanese film database: Daiei film directed by Kurosawa, released in Japan 25/26 August 1950. US release 26 Dec 1951; Venice Golden Lion 1951.

title: Alien
author: Ridley Scott
note: Second search (first named no director): film pages say directed by Ridley Scott, US release 25 May 1979 (wide 22 June), 20th Century Fox. Screenplay Dan O'Bannon.

title: Auntie Mame
author: Patrick Dennis (Edward Everett Tanner III)
note: Wikipedia: Vanguard Press, 21 January 1955; Goodreads says 1 December 1955 (day differs, year same). Dennis was born Edward Everett Tanner III.

title: Carmina
author: Catullus
note: Wikipedia and Gutenberg: poems written 62-54 BC, latest datable ones c. 55 BC. No publication date given; the book was arranged by Catullus. c. 55 BCE is inside the range.

title: Darkness Visible
author: William Styron
note: Wikipedia and catalogue records: Random House book 1990 (84 pp), expanded from a Dec 1989 Vanity Fair essay. Library year is the book edition.

title: Novel on Yellow Paper
author: Stevie Smith
note: Wikipedia and Hachette page: first published 1936 (her first novel). Hull History Centre says Jonathan Cape published it.

title: Chanson de Roland
author: Anonymous
note: Wikipedia/New World Encyclopedia: composed late 11th c. (range 1040-1115). Oldest manuscript Digby 23 (Oxford) c. 1129-1170. Poet 'Turoldus' named in text, attribution uncertain.

title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court
author: Mark Twain
note: Britannica/encyclopedia and rare-book dealer results give 1889 (Chatto & Windus Dec 1889 UK; Webster, New York, 1889); sources differ on which edition was first, same year.

title: A Journal of the Plague Year
author: Daniel Defoe
note: Wikipedia and library records: first published March 1722, originally signed H. F. One library catalogue says 1723, apparently an error.

title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built
author: Becky Chambers
note: Wikipedia plus publisher/bookseller/NPR-GPB results: Tordotcom, 13 July 2021, Monk & Robot #1 by Becky Chambers. (Needed a second search to see the author named.)

title: A Room of One's Own
author: Virginia Woolf
note: Retailer/library/dealer results: Hogarth Press, 24 Oct 1929 (some give Sept); based on Oct 1928 lectures at Newnham and Girton. US edition Harcourt Brace.

title: A Writer's Diary
author: Virginia Woolf
note: Morgan Library and NYPL catalogues: Hogarth Press, London, Nov 1953; extracts from Woolf's diary chosen and edited by Leonard Woolf. Full diaries came 1977-84.

title: Abhijnanasakuntalam (The Recognition of Shakuntala)
author: Kalidasa
note: Study-guide and Wikipedia-derived pages: Kalidasa usually placed 4th c. CE but dates much disputed (wider ranges given); c. 400 CE is within the common estimate. No firm date exists.

title: Absalom and Achitophel
author: John Dryden
note: Britannica and Wikipedia: verse satire by John Dryden published 1681; Part II (mostly Nahum Tate) followed in 1682.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
author: Mark Twain
note: Wikipedia-derived text and catalogues: first UK publication Dec 1884, US Feb 1885; Gutenberg says 1884-1885. 1884 is correct for first publication (UK).

title: Against Interpretation
author: Susan Sontag
note: Wikipedia/Penguin/Goodreads: collection first published 1966 by Farrar, Straus and Giroux. (From memory the title essay ran in 1964; not seen in results.)

title: An Essay on Man
author: Alexander Pope
note: Britannica/Wikipedia/catalogue: epistles I-III 1733, IV 1734, published anonymously; one edition intro says 1732-34. Library range 1733-34 fits.

title: Andha Yug
author: Dharamvir Bharati
note: Outlook India and Wikipedia lead: 1953; Wikipedia infobox and Goodreads: written/first published 1954; premiere 1962. Library's 1953/1954 matches the disagreement.

title: As I Lay Dying
author: William Faulkner
note: Wikipedia and rare-book dealer pages: first published 6 Oct 1930 (Jonathan Cape & Harrison Smith, New York); written in 1929. UK Chatto edition 1935.

title: Arabesques
author: Anton Shammas
note: NYRB, Yale Review and Jewish Currents: Hebrew original Arabeskot first published 1986; English translation (Vivian Eden) 1988, reissued NYRB Classics 2023.

title: I Is a Long-Memoried Woman
author: Grace Nichols
note: UNC library record and publisher page (Karnak House): 1983; her first poetry collection, won the Commonwealth Poetry Prize that year.

title: Seven Brief Lessons on Physics
author: Carlo Rovelli
note: Wikipedia and catalogue records: Italian original Sette brevi lezioni di fisica, Adelphi, Milan, 2014; English (Allen Lane, tr. Segre/Carnell) 2015. Needed second search to see author named.

title: Rich Man, Poor Man
author: Irwin Shaw
note: Sources disagree: Wikipedia infobox and Goodreads give Delacorte, Sept 1970; Wikipedia lead and UVA bestsellers database say 1969. From memory 1970 is the usual first-edition date.
resolution: Sources split: 1969 (copyright; a university bestseller database) and 1970 (library catalogue records, one infobox). The library keeps 1969; not resolved.

title: The Plague Prayers of Mursili II
author: Mursili II
note: Scholarly and popular pages date prayers to Mursili's reign c. 1321-1295 BCE, plague c. 1320-1300 BCE; c. 1300 BCE fits. Authorship is the king's by tradition.

title: The Unwomanly Face of War
author: Svetlana Alexievich
note: Penguin and library records: Russian original 1985 (Moscow/Minsk, publisher differs); first English 1988 as War's Unwomanly Face; 2017 Pevear/Volokhonsky translation.

title: Chunhyangga
author: Traditional (pansori repertoire)
sourceYear: no firm date; attested by late 17th-18th c.
note: Wikipedia-derived pages: no record of composition date or author; oral pansori tale known by the Joseon era (before 1720). Library gives no year and a traditional author, consistent.

title: L'Art poétique
author: Nicolas Boileau
note: Wikipedia and Britannica: didactic poem in four cantos published 1674 in Boileau's Oeuvres diverses alongside Le Lutrin.

title: She
author: H. Rider Haggard
note: Wikipedia: serialised in The Graphic from 2 Oct 1886 to 7 Jan 1887; US book (Harper) 24 Dec 1886, UK book (Longmans) 1 Jan 1887. 1887 is the usual book date; serial-vs-book difference.
resolution: The library gives the usual book date (1887); the serial began in October 1886 and the first book edition was December 1886. Left as is.

title: Stuck Rubber Baby
author: Howard Cruse
note: Wikipedia, Publishers Weekly: graphic novel first published 1995 by Paradox Press (DC Comics imprint); paperback HarperCollins 1996; First Second 25th anniversary 2020.

title: Before I Go to Sleep
author: S. J. Watson
note: Wikipedia and BookBrowse: debut novel, UK April 2011 (Doubleday), US June 2011 (HarperCollins).

title: Cántico
author: Jorge Guillén
note: Encyclopedic/biographical results: first edition of 75 poems, Madrid, Revista de Occidente, 1928; expanded in 1936, 1945, 1950 (334 poems).
